question: Will Mark Lamb be the Republican nominee for AZ-05?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Republican Party to contest the AZ-05 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Republican primary will take place on August 4, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Republican sources, including https://www.rnc.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

evidence.excerpt: Club for Growth PAC reported a poll showing Mark Lamb at 61%, Daniel Keenan at 27%, and 12% undecided in the AZ-05 Republican primary. The organization, which supports Lamb, also announced that its affiliated Win It Back PAC was releasing an advertisement emphasizing Donald Trump's endorsement. The release said the $250,000 television advertising campaign would begin July 7 on Fox News, satellite, and streaming.

The Pinal County Attorney's Office closed its review of allegations involving former Sheriff Mark Lamb after determining that the evidence reviewed did not establish a violation of Arizona criminal law. The office reviewed records, witness statements, text messages, social media posts, recorded calls, and other communications. County Attorney Brad Miller wrote that the materials provided showed no acts by Lamb that would be considered criminal under Arizona law.

Lamb continued campaigning with Trump's endorsement while some Republicans distanced themselves following reports about sexually explicit messages, threats, and racist language. Opponent Daniel Keenan was running a television advertisement attacking Lamb's fitness for office. Cook Political Report analyst Matthew Klein said Trump's rescission of endorsements was rare and that Lamb's loyalty to Trump made withdrawal of support difficult to envision.

Daniel Keenan and Mark Lamb were running in the Republican primary for Arizona's 5th Congressional District, with incumbent Andy Biggs seeking the governorship instead of reelection. As of March 31, 2026, Keenan had raised $1,578,351 compared with Lamb's $759,707. Keenan led in fundraising, while Lamb led in noteworthy endorsements.

evidence.publisher: The Arizona Republic, republished by the Arizona Daily Star
evidence.excerpt: Allegations of threatening women, sexual impropriety, and racist comments disrupted Lamb's congressional campaign and prompted calls for him to leave the race. Andy Biggs described the allegations through a spokesperson as concerning, while David Schweikert said Lamb must explain himself or drop out. Keenan released a video advertisement displaying screenshots published by The Arizona Republic.

Following passage of HB2022, Secretary of State Adrian Fontes announced a new primary election date of July 21, 2026. The updated timeline set June 22 as the voter registration deadline, June 24 as the beginning of early voting, and July 10 as the last day to request a ballot by mail.

President Donald Trump endorsed former Pinal County Sheriff Mark Lamb in the race to replace Andy Biggs in Arizona's 5th Congressional District. Trump gave Lamb his complete and total endorsement and encouraged rival Jay Feely to run in a different district or for another office. Biggs was foregoing reelection to run for governor.
